uwadmin: Somewhere right now there's an underwriter who can price a risk in ten minutes, and spends the day typing it into three different places.
You retype the proposal form. You wait three days for a referral. And the file you are rating has no history on it.
We are opening a general insurance agency, here in Chaguanas.
Motor, property, liability, engineering, marine and bonds. A real commercial book.
Before you open a file, every term since the policy began is already on the screen. What was covered, at what value, what was paid, and the claims that fell in each term.
The insurer's notice is read for you, and every figure is checked against our own record. Where the two disagree, the desk says so.
Here is the part most underwriters never get. A rule you decide is not a ticket at head office. It is written into the desk, and it runs on every file that week.
Your own referral rules. A flag that fires when the declared value stops moving. A rating check the client never has to ask for.
The paperwork is finished. The underwriting is not. That is the job.
One underwriting seat. Chaguanas. Come and build the book.
